title: Halve the pretraining batch from 256 to 128 records under the Muon incumbent (more optimizer steps, same wall-clock)
description: Batch-size ablation, not a backlog P-idea (nearest: none; P02 Muon incumbent context): change only BS 256 -> 128 in 064-claude's pretrain.py, keeping every per-step hyperparameter, so the fixed 300 s wall-clock buys ~1.8x more optimizer steps (~4,200 vs 2,339) at roughly the same records seen (~3.6-3.9 epochs). 007 (bs 512, AdamW, old protocol) halved the step count and collapsed the metric (23 vs 56-67), which says the loop sits at or above the critical batch size at 256, so halving the batch should buy nearly 2x the optimization progress per record and hand expert iteration a sharper proof prior without the extra epochs that made 002's samples run away.
hypothesis: Step time is compute-bound and roughly linear in batch size (007: 2x batch -> 2.16x fewer steps), so BS 128 gives ~1.8x the Muon/AdamW updates for the same data. Muon's orthogonalized update has a fixed spectral size per step regardless of batch, and momentum 0.95 averages ~20 steps (~2,500 records) so the extra gradient noise is largely smoothed; if 256 is at or above the critical batch (as 007's collapse implies), more, smaller steps move the weights further along the same wall-clock cosine and reach lower loss / better-formed proof-step features. Because epochs are not increased (unlike 002), the handoff model should not become more overconfident; better Stage-1 competence should raise round-1 sample accuracy on >=7-line targets and compound through the four EI rounds. Counter-risks: noisier final checkpoint at the 0.1 LR floor, twice the total weight decay, 200-step warmup now shorter in wall-clock, and ~6% more relative per-step overhead (Newton-Schulz, Python) eating into records seen.
expected_delta: -40 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central ~0); pretrain steps ~4,000-4,500 (vs 2,339); final val loss 0.085-0.095 (064: 0.0912)

arch.change: none versus 064-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 064-claude)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction; head.weight therefore keeps the same per-step multiplicative decay it had under AdamW.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

batch.change: 256 -> 128 records per optimizer step; the only edit to pretrain.py (the BS knob). No LR, warmup-step, momentum, decay or clipping rescaling: all per-step hyperparameters are exactly 064-claude's.
batch.consequences: WARMUP stays 200 optimizer steps (now roughly half the wall-clock it took at 256); the wall-clock cosine is unchanged; per-step weight decay is unchanged, so total decay over the run grows with the step count; val_loss is computed in batches of 128 instead of 256 (diagnostic only).

config.init: Exactly 064-claude/051: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights per seed identical to 064-claude; data order/shift RNG streams differ because batches are half as large.
